sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yudhiṣṭhirasya tad vākyaṃ śrutvā bhīṣmo mahāmanāḥ parīkṣya nipuṇaṃ buddhyā yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard those words of Yudhiṣṭhira, the great-souled Bhīṣma, after examining Yudhiṣṭhira keenly with his discerning mind, spoke to him.

sanskrit: rahasyam adbhutaṃ caiva śṛṇu vakṣyāmi yat tvayi yā gatiḥ prāpyate yena pretyabhāveṣu bhārata
english: Hear the secret and the wondrous thing that I shall declare to you, O descendant of Bharata—by what means a man attains his destined state in the conditions that follow death.

sanskrit: tapasā prāpyate svargas tapasā prāpyate yaśaḥ āyuḥprakarṣo bhogāś ca labhyante tapasā vibho
english: By austerity heaven is won, by austerity fame is won; length of life and enjoyments too are gained by austerity, O mighty one.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ vijñānam ārogyaṃ rūpaṃ saṃpat tathaiva ca saubhāgyaṃ caiva tapasā prāpyate bharatarṣabha
english: Knowledge, discernment, health, beauty, prosperity, and good fortune as well—all these are attained by austerity, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: dhanaṃ prāpnoti tapasā maunaṃ jñānaṃ prayacchati upabhogāṃs tu dānena brahmacaryeṇa jīvitam
english: By austerity one obtains wealth; silence bestows knowledge; enjoyments come through giving, and long life through chastity.

sanskrit: ahiṃsāyāḥ phalaṃ rūpaṃ dīkṣāyā janma vai kule phalamūlāśināṃ rājyaṃ svargaḥ parṇāśināṃ bhavet
english: Beauty is the fruit of non-injury; birth in a noble lineage the fruit of sacred vows; a kingdom befalls those who feed on fruits and roots, and heaven those who feed on leaves.

sanskrit: payobhakṣo divaṃ yāti snānena draviṇādhikaḥ guruśuśrūṣayā vidyā nityaśrāddhena saṃtatiḥ
english: He who lives on milk goes to heaven; by ritual bathing one grows rich in possessions; by service to the teacher comes learning, and by constant offerings to the ancestors comes progeny.

sanskrit: gavāḍhyaḥ śākadīkṣābhiḥ svargam āhus tṛṇāśanāt striyas triṣavaṇasnānād vāyuṃ pītvā kratuṃ labhet
english: By vows of eating only herbs a man becomes rich in cattle; from feeding on grass, they say, comes heaven; from bathing at the three pressings come women, and by drinking only air one gains the merit of a sacrifice.

sanskrit: nityasnāyī bhaved dakṣaḥ saṃdhye tu dve japan dvijaḥ maruṃ sādhayato rājyaṃ nākapṛṣṭham anāśake
english: By bathing daily one becomes capable; the twice-born who murmurs his prayers at the two twilights wins a kingdom by mastering the desert wilds, and the vault of heaven by total fasting.

sanskrit: sthaṇḍile śayamānānāṃ gṛhāṇi śayanāni ca cīravalkalavāsobhir vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca
english: For those who sleep upon the bare ground there come houses and couches; through garments of rags and bark come fine robes and ornaments.

sanskrit: śayyāsanāni yānāni yogayukte tapodhane agnipraveśe niyataṃ brahmaloko vidhīyate
english: For the ascetic rich in penance and joined to discipline come beds, seats, and chariots; for one who enters the fire, the world of Brahmā is surely ordained.

sanskrit: rasānāṃ pratisaṃhārāt saubhāgyam iha vindati āmiṣapratisaṃhārāt prajāsyāyuṣmatī bhavet
english: By renouncing savory delicacies one finds good fortune here; by abstaining from flesh one's offspring become long-lived.

sanskrit: udavāsaṃ vased yas tu sa narādhipatir bhavet satyavādī naraśreṣṭha daivataiḥ saha modate
english: He who dwells standing in water becomes a lord of men; the truth-speaker, O best of men, rejoices in the company of the gods.

sanskrit: kīrtir bhavati dānena tathārogyam ahiṃsayā dvijaśuśrūṣayā rājyaṃ dvijatvaṃ vāpi puṣkalam
english: Renown comes through giving, and health through non-injury; by service to the twice-born comes a kingdom, or else abundant twice-born status itself.

sanskrit: pānīyasya pradānena kīrtir bhavati śāśvatī annapānapradānena tṛpyate kāmabhogataḥ
english: By the gift of water one's fame becomes everlasting; by the gift of food and drink one is sated to the full in the enjoyment of one's desires.

sanskrit: sāntvadaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvaśokair vimucyate devaśuśrūṣayā rājyaṃ divyaṃ rūpaṃ niyacchati
english: He who speaks gently to all beings is freed from every sorrow; service to the gods bestows a kingdom and a celestial beauty.

sanskrit: dīpālokapradānena cakṣuṣmān bhavate naraḥ prekṣaṇīyapradānena smṛtiṃ medhāṃ ca vindati
english: By the gift of lamplight a man becomes endowed with keen sight; by the gift of fair spectacles he attains memory and intelligence.

sanskrit: gandhamālyanivṛttyā tu kīrtir bhavati puṣkalā keśaśmaśrūn dhārayatām agryā bhavati saṃtatiḥ
english: By abstaining from perfumes and garlands one's renown grows abundant; for those who let their hair and beard grow there comes excellent progeny.

sanskrit: upavāsaṃ ca dīkṣāṃ ca abhiṣekaṃ ca pārthiva kṛtvā dvādaśa varṣāṇi vīrasthānād viśiṣyate
english: He who keeps fasting, the sacred vow, and ablution for twelve years, O king, surpasses even the abode of heroes.

sanskrit: dāsīdāsam alaṃkārān kṣetrāṇi ca gṛhāṇi ca brahmadeyāṃ sutāṃ dattvā prāpnoti manujarṣabha
english: By giving a daughter in righteous marriage—along with maidservants and menservants, ornaments, fields, and houses—a man obtains them all in turn, O bull among men.

sanskrit: kratubhiś copavāsaiś ca tridivaṃ yāti bhārata labhate ca ciraṃ sthānaṃ balipuṣpaprado naraḥ
english: By sacrifices and fasts a man goes to the triple heaven, O descendant of Bharata; and the man who offers oblations and flowers gains an enduring station.

sanskrit: suvarṇaśṛṅgais tu vibhūṣitānāṃ; gavāṃ sahasrasya naraḥ pradātā prāpnoti puṇyaṃ divi devalokam; ity evam āhur munidevasaṃghāḥ
english: The man who bestows a thousand cows adorned with golden horns attains the blessed world of the gods in heaven—so declare the assembled sages and deities.

sanskrit: prayacchate yaḥ kapilāṃ sacailāṃ; kāṃsyopadohāṃ kanakāgraśṛṅgīm tais tair guṇaiḥ kāmadughāsya bhūtvā; naraṃ pradātāram upaiti sā gauḥ
english: To him who gives a tawny cow draped in cloth, with a bronze milking-vessel and gold-tipped horns, that cow—becoming for him a fulfiller of every wish by all those virtues—returns to the man who gave her.

sanskrit: yāvanti lomāni bhavanti dhenvās; tāvat phalaṃ prāpnute gopradātā putrāṃś ca pautrāṃś ca kulaṃ ca sarvam; āsaptamaṃ tārayate paratra
english: As many as are the hairs upon the cow, so great is the reward the giver of cattle obtains; and he delivers his sons, his grandsons, and his whole line down to the seventh generation in the world beyond.

sanskrit: sadakṣiṇāṃ kāñcanacāruśṛṅgīṃ; kāṃsyopadohāṃ draviṇottarīyām dhenuṃ tilānāṃ dadato dvijāya; lokā vasūnāṃ sulabhā bhavanti
english: For one who gives to a twice-born a cow of sesame, complete with priestly fee, with fair golden horns, a bronze milking-vessel, and a covering of wealth, the worlds of the Vasus become easy to win.

sanskrit: svakarmabhir mānavaṃ saṃnibaddhaṃ; tīvrāndhakāre narake patantam mahārṇave naur iva vāyuyuktā; dānaṃ gavāṃ tārayate paratra
english: As a ship driven by the wind across the great ocean, so the gift of cattle carries a man across to the world beyond—a man bound fast by his own deeds and falling into a hell of dense darkness.

sanskrit: yo brahmadeyāṃ tu dadāti kanyāṃ; bhūmipradānaṃ ca karoti vipre dadāti cānnaṃ vidhivac ca yaś ca; sa lokam āpnoti puraṃdarasya
english: He who gives a maiden in righteous marriage, who bestows land upon a brāhmaṇa, and who gives food according to the rite—he attains the world of Puraṃdara.

sanskrit: naiveśikaṃ sarvaguṇopapannaṃ; dadāti vai yas tu naro dvijāya svādhyāyacāritraguṇānvitāya; tasyāpi lokāḥ kuruṣūttareṣu
english: The man who gives a dwelling endowed with every comfort to a twice-born adorned with the virtues of sacred study and good conduct—for him too the worlds in the northern Kurus are won.

sanskrit: dhuryapradānena gavāṃ tathāśvair; lokān avāpnoti naro vasūnām svargāya cāhur hi hiraṇyadānaṃ; tato viśiṣṭaṃ kanakapradānam
english: By the gift of draught-oxen and likewise of cattle and horses, a man attains the worlds of the Vasus; and they say the gift of silver leads to heaven, while the gift of gold is more excellent still.

sanskrit: chatrapradānena gṛhaṃ variṣṭhaṃ; yānaṃ tathopānahasaṃpradāne vastrapradānena phalaṃ surūpaṃ; gandhapradāne surabhir naraḥ syāt
english: By the gift of a parasol comes an excellent house; by the gift of footwear, a chariot; by the gift of garments, the fruit of beauty; and by the gift of perfumes a man becomes fragrant.

sanskrit: puṣpopagaṃ vātha phalopagaṃ vā; yaḥ pādapaṃ sparśayate dvijāya sa strīsamṛddhaṃ bahuratnapūrṇaṃ; labhaty ayatnopagataṃ gṛhaṃ vai
english: He who bestows upon a twice-born a tree laden with flowers or with fruit gains, without effort, a house rich in women and filled with many jewels.

sanskrit: bhakṣānnapānīyarasapradātā; sarvān avāpnoti rasān prakāmam pratiśrayācchādanasaṃpradātā; prāpnoti tān eva na saṃśayo 'tra
english: The giver of food, drink, water, and savory dishes obtains all delights to his heart's content; and the giver of shelter and clothing obtains those very same—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: sragdhūpagandhāny anulepanāni; snānāni mālyāni ca mānavo yaḥ dadyād dvijebhyaḥ sa bhaved arogas; tathābhirūpaś ca narendraloke
english: The man who gives to the twice-born wreaths, incense, perfumes, unguents, bathing-materials, and garlands becomes free from disease, and likewise comely, in the world of kings.

sanskrit: bījair aśūnyaṃ śayanair upetaṃ; dadyād gṛhaṃ yaḥ puruṣo dvijāya puṇyābhirāmaṃ bahuratnapūrṇaṃ; labhaty adhiṣṭhānavaraṃ sa rājan
english: The man who gives to a twice-born a house not empty of seed and furnished with couches gains, O king, an excellent abode, holy and delightful and filled with many jewels.

sanskrit: sugandhacitrāstaraṇopapannaṃ; dadyān naro yaḥ śayanaṃ dvijāya rūpānvitāṃ pakṣavatīṃ manojñāṃ; bhāryām ayatnopagatāṃ labhet saḥ
english: The man who gives to a twice-born a bed furnished with fragrant and richly patterned coverings gains, without effort, a wife endowed with beauty, well-supported by kin, and pleasing to the heart.

sanskrit: pitāmahasyānucaro vīraśāyī bhaven naraḥ nādhikaṃ vidyate tasmād ity āhuḥ paramarṣayaḥ
english: The man who lies down to die as a hero becomes a follower of the Grandsire; than this there is nothing higher—so declare the supreme seers.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā prītātmā kurunandanaḥ nāśrame 'rocayad vāsaṃ vīramārgābhikāṅkṣayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard those words of his, the delighted son of the Kurus no longer favored dwelling in a hermitage, longing instead for the path of the hero.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prāha pāṇḍavān bharatarṣabha pitāmahasya yad vākyaṃ tad vo rocatv iti prabhuḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, the bull of the Bhāratas, that lord addressed the Pāṇḍavas: "Let the words of the Grandsire find favor with you."

sanskrit: tatas tu pāṇḍavāḥ sarve draupadī ca yaśasvinī yudhiṣṭhirasya tad vākyaṃ bāḍham ity abhyapūjayan
english: Thereupon all the Pāṇḍavas, and the illustrious Draupadī, honored those words of Yudhiṣṭhira, saying, "So be it."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yānīmāni bahir vedyāṃ dānāni paricakṣate tebhyo viśiṣṭaṃ kiṃ dānaṃ mataṃ te kurupuṃgava
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Among those gifts that are reckoned as made outside the sacrificial altar, which gift do you hold to be the most excellent, O foremost of the Kurus?

sanskrit: kautūhalaṃ hi paramaṃ tatra me vartate prabho dātāraṃ dattam anveti yad dānaṃ tat pracakṣva me
english: For my curiosity in this matter is very great, O lord: declare to me that gift whose merit follows after the giver.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo vyasane cāpy anugraham yac cābhilaṣitaṃ dadyāt tṛṣitāyābhiyācate
english: Bhīṣma said: Freedom from fear granted to all beings, and aid given in time of distress; and that which one gives, the very thing he longs for, to a thirsting suppliant who begs—

sanskrit: dattaṃ manyeta yad dattvā tad dānaṃ śreṣṭham ucyate dattaṃ dātāram anveti yad dānaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: that gift, after giving which one feels he has truly given, is called the best; for it is the gift whose merit follows after the giver, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: hiraṇyadānaṃ godānaṃ pṛthivīdānam eva ca etāni vai pavitrāṇi tārayanty api duṣkṛtam
english: The gift of gold, the gift of cattle, and the gift of land—these indeed are purifying, and they carry across even the doer of evil.

sanskrit: etāni puruṣavyāghra sādhubhyo dehi nityadā dānāni hi naraṃ pāpān mokṣayanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: Give these always to the virtuous, O tiger among men; for gifts release a man from sin—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yad yad iṣṭatamaṃ loke yac cāsya dayitaṃ gṛhe tat tad guṇavate deyaṃ tad evākṣayam icchatā
english: Whatever is most cherished in the world, and whatever is most beloved in one's own house—that should be given to a worthy man by one who desires it to become imperishable.

sanskrit: priyāṇi labhate loke priyadaḥ priyakṛt tathā priyo bhavati bhūtānām iha caiva paratra ca
english: He who gives what is dear and does what is dear obtains dear things in the world, and becomes beloved of all beings both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: yācamānam abhīmānād āśāvantam akiṃcanam yo nārcati yathāśakti sa nṛśaṃso yudhiṣṭhira
english: He who, out of pride, does not honor to the best of his power a suppliant who begs—one full of hope and possessing nothing—that man is cruel, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: amitram api ced dīnaṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇam āgatam vyasane yo 'nugṛhṇāti sa vai puruṣasattamaḥ
english: He who shows favor in time of distress even to an enemy who comes wretched and seeking refuge—he indeed is the best of men.

sanskrit: kṛśāya hrīmate tāta vṛttikṣīṇāya sīdate apahanyāt kṣudhaṃ yas tu na tena puruṣaḥ samaḥ
english: To the gaunt and modest man, my son, ruined in his livelihood and sinking down—he who drives away that man's hunger, no other man is his equal.

sanskrit: hriyā tu niyatān sādhūn putradāraiś ca karśitān ayācamānān kaunteya sarvopāyair nimantraya
english: The virtuous who are held back by modesty, worn thin with the care of wives and children, and who do not beg—these, O son of Kuntī, invite by every means.

sanskrit: āśiṣaṃ ye na deveṣu na martyeṣu ca kurvate arhanto nityasattvasthā yathālabdhopajīvinaḥ
english: Those who make no entreaty either to the gods or to mortals—worthy men, ever fixed in goodness, living on whatever they happen to obtain—

sanskrit: āśīviṣasamebhyaś ca tebhyo rakṣasva bhārata tāny uktair upajijñāsya tathā dvijavarottamān
english: guard yourself against such men, who are like venomous serpents, O descendant of Bharata; sound out those most excellent of the twice-born with respectful words.

sanskrit: kṛtair āvasathair nityaṃ sapreṣyaiḥ saparicchadaiḥ nimantrayethāḥ kauravya sarvakāmasukhāvahaiḥ
english: Invite them ever, O scion of Kuru, with dwellings made ready, complete with servants and furnishings, that bring every desire and comfort.

sanskrit: yadi te pratigṛhṇīyuḥ śraddhāpūtaṃ yudhiṣṭhira kāryam ity eva manvānā dhārmikāḥ puṇyakarmiṇaḥ
english: If those righteous men of holy deeds should accept what is hallowed by faith, O Yudhiṣṭhira, deeming it merely a duty to be done—

sanskrit: vidyāsnātā vratasnātā ye vyapāśrityajīvinaḥ gūḍhasvādhyāyatapaso brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: those brāhmaṇas accomplished in learning, accomplished in vows, who live without dependence on others, whose private study and austerity are hidden, and whose vows are firmly held—

sanskrit: teṣu śuddheṣu dānteṣu svadāranirateṣu ca yat kariṣyasi kalyāṇaṃ tat tvā lokeṣu dhāsyati
english: whatever good you do to them—the pure, the self-controlled, devoted to their own wives—that will establish you in the higher worlds.

sanskrit: yathāgnihotraṃ suhutaṃ sāyaṃ prātar dvijātinā tathā bhavati dattaṃ vai dvijebhyo 'tha kṛtātmanā
english: As the fire-oblation well offered evening and morning by the twice-born, so does the gift given to the twice-born by a man of disciplined soul become.

sanskrit: eṣa te vitato yajñaḥ śraddhāpūtaḥ sadakṣiṇaḥ viśiṣṭaḥ sarvayajñebhyo dadatas tāta vartatām
english: This is your sacrifice spread out, hallowed by faith and furnished with priestly fees—surpassing all other sacrifices. Let it proceed, my son, as you give.

sanskrit: nivāpo dānasadṛśas tādṛśeṣu yudhiṣṭhira nivapan pūjayaṃś caiva teṣv ānṛṇyaṃ nigacchati
english: An offering to the ancestors is like a gift when made to such men, O Yudhiṣṭhira; by making such offerings and honoring them, one is freed of his debt to them.

sanskrit: ya eva no na kupyanti na lubhyanti tṛṇeṣv api ta eva naḥ pūjyatamā ye cānye priyavādinaḥ
english: Those who are never angry with us and never covet even so much as a blade of grass—they are the most worthy of our reverence, and likewise the others who speak kindly.

sanskrit: ye no na bahu manyante na pravartanti cāpare putravat paripālyās te namas tebhyas tathābhayam
english: Those others who do not think much of us and do not press themselves forward—they too are to be cherished like one's own sons; reverence to them, and to them freedom from fear.

sanskrit: ṛtvikpurohitācāryā mṛdubrahmadharā hi te kṣatreṇāpi hi saṃsṛṣṭaṃ tejaḥ śāmyati vai dvije
english: The officiating priest, the household chaplain, and the teacher—these bear the sacred power gently; for even the splendor mingled with kṣatriya might is quenched in the twice-born.

sanskrit: asti me balavān asmi rājāsmīti yudhiṣṭhira brāhmaṇān mā sma paryaśnīr vāsobhir aśanena ca
english: Thinking "I have wealth, I am mighty, I am king," do not, O Yudhiṣṭhira, slight the brāhmaṇas in the matter of garments and of food.

sanskrit: yac chobhārthaṃ balārthaṃ vā vittam asti tavānagha tena te brāhmaṇāḥ pūjyāḥ svadharmam anutiṣṭhatā
english: Whatever wealth you have for the sake of splendor or of strength, O sinless one, with it the brāhmaṇas are to be honored by you who follow your own duty.

sanskrit: namaskāryās tvayā viprā vartamānā yathātatham yathāsukhaṃ yathotsāhaṃ lalantu tvayi putravat
english: The brāhmaṇas, living rightly according to truth, are to be saluted by you; let them take their pleasure in you to their ease and to their delight, as sons do with a father.

sanskrit: ko hy anyaḥ suprasādānāṃ suhṛdām alpatoṣiṇām vṛttim arhaty upakṣeptuṃ tvad anyaḥ kurusattama
english: For who else but you, O best of the Kurus, is fit to provide the maintenance of these gracious friends who are content with little?

sanskrit: yathā patyāśrayo dharmaḥ strīṇāṃ loke sanātanaḥ sa devaḥ sā gatir nānyā tathāsmākaṃ dvijātayaḥ
english: As the duty of women in the world is eternally to take refuge in their husband—he is their god, he their sole recourse and no other—so are the twice-born to us.

sanskrit: yadi no brāhmaṇās tāta saṃtyajeyur apūjitāḥ paśyanto dāruṇaṃ karma satataṃ kṣatriye sthitam
english: If the brāhmaṇas, dishonored, should forsake us, my son—seeing the cruel deeds that ever attend the kṣatriya—

sanskrit: avedānām akīrtīnām alokānām ayajvanām ko 'smākaṃ jīvitenārthas tad dhi no brāhmaṇāśrayam
english: then, bereft of the Veda, of fame, of the higher worlds, and of sacrifice, what use is life to us? For that all rests upon our recourse to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi yathā dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ rājanyo brāhmaṇaṃ rājan purā paricacāra ha vaiśyo rājanyam ity eva śūdro vaiśyam iti śrutiḥ
english: On this I shall expound to you what the eternal law is. In olden days the kṣatriya waited upon the brāhmaṇa, O king, the vaiśya upon the kṣatriya, and the śūdra upon the vaiśya—so runs the sacred tradition.

sanskrit: dūrāc chūdreṇopacaryo brāhmaṇo 'gnir iva jvalan saṃsparśaparicaryas tu vaiśyena kṣatriyeṇa ca
english: The brāhmaṇa, blazing like fire, is to be served by the śūdra from a distance, but he may be served with touch by the vaiśya and by the kṣatriya.

sanskrit: mṛdubhāvān satyaśīlān satyadharmānupālakān āśīviṣān iva kruddhāṃs tān upācarata dvijān
english: Attend upon those twice-born, who are gentle of nature, truthful in conduct, and guardians of the law of truth, yet who when angered are like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: apareṣāṃ pareṣāṃ ca parebhyaś caiva ye pare kṣatriyāṇāṃ pratapatāṃ tejasā ca balena ca brāhmaṇeṣv eva śāmyanti tejāṃsi ca tapāṃsi ca
english: The fiery energies and austerities of the kṣatriyas who burn with splendor and might—surpassing some, surpassing others, surpassing even those beyond the rest—are quelled in the brāhmaṇas alone.

sanskrit: na me pitā priyataro na tvaṃ tāta tathā priyaḥ na me pituḥ pitā rājan na cātmā na ca jīvitam
english: Not my father is dearer to me, nor are you, my son, so dear, nor my father's father, O king, nor my own self, nor my life—

sanskrit: tvattaś ca me priyataraḥ pṛthivyāṃ nāsti kaś cana tvatto 'pi me priyatarā brāhmaṇā bharatarṣabha
english: and though there is none on earth dearer to me than you, yet even dearer to me than you, O bull of the Bhāratas, are the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: bravīmi satyam etac ca yathāhaṃ pāṇḍunandana tena satyena gaccheyaṃ lokān yatra sa śaṃtanuḥ
english: This truth I speak, O joy of Pāṇḍu, just as it is; and by that truth may I go to those worlds where Śaṃtanu dwells.

sanskrit: paśyeyaṃ ca satāṃ lokāñ chucīn brahmapuraskṛtān tatra me tāta gantavyam ahnāya ca cirāya ca
english: And may I behold the pure worlds of the good, with the sacred power set foremost; thither, my son, I must go, both soon and for long to come.

sanskrit: so 'ham etādṛśāṃl lokān dṛṣṭvā bharatasattama yan me kṛtaṃ brāhmaṇeṣu na tapye tena pārthiva
english: And I, having beheld such worlds, O best of the Bhāratas, do not repent of what I have done for the brāhmaṇas, O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yau tu syātāṃ caraṇenopapannau; yau vidyayā sadṛśau janmanā ca tābhyāṃ dānaṃ katarasmai viśiṣṭam; ayācamānāya ca yācate ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of two men who are alike endowed with good conduct, and equal in learning and in birth—to which of these is the gift more excellent, to the one who does not beg or to the one who begs?
